# 🍺 Tavern Wagers [![test](https://github.com/bardhojorgo22-beep/wagers/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/bardhojorgo22-beep/wagers/actions/workflows/test.yml) ![Tavern Wagers](web/cover.png) **Bet on anything with your friends. The money's locked upfront, neutral judges call it, and the winner gets paid automatically. No more "I'll pay you later."** Built on [Gno.land](https://gno.land) for the Gnome Tavern hackathon. **Try it in 60 seconds:** open the [web app](https://tavern-wagers.vercel.app). It shows sample data (demo mode) while the testnet package waits for approval: open *Friday Chess Club*, then the disputed *Darts, best of 3* bet and the *Friday poker night* group bet. **Web app:** https://tavern-wagers.vercel.app · **Realm:** https://onyx.testnets.gno.land/r/g1sgp0eyezdescdtzd32n2vdktazva4nyt9ppmcx/tavernwagers/v5 ## The problem Friendly bets ("I'll beat you at chess", "Arsenal wins Saturday") break down in three ways: 1. **The loser doesn't pay.** "I'll pay you later" turns into never. 2. **Someone has to hold the pot**, and everyone has to trust them. 3. **Arguments about who won.** Two people, two different stories. ## How Tavern Wagers fixes it | Problem | Fix | |---|---| | Loser doesn't pay | Both players lock their stake in the realm **before** the game. Payout is automatic. | | Someone holds the pot | Nobody does. The realm holds it, and its code is public. | | Arguments about who won | Everyone else at the table becomes a **judge**. Judges have no money in the bet, so they have no reason to lie. | | People lie anyway | Each player also locks a **10% honesty bond**. Lose the judges' vote and you lose your bond, plus a permanent 🚩 on the leaderboard. | The realm takes **no cut**. Every coin that goes in comes back out to players and judges. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Open a table, add friends] --> B[Player A challenges B
locks stake + 10% bond] B -->|B declines| X[Refund A] B -->|B accepts, locks the same
judges are fixed now| C[Game on] C --> D{Both players report} D -->|same result| E[Instant payout
bonds back, no fee] D -->|different results
or a no-show after 24h| F[Judges vote
table members not playing] F -->|strict majority| G[Payout minus 1% judge fee
liar loses bond + 🚩] F -->|no majority in 48h| H[Full refund, bonds included] ``` 1. **Open a table** and add your friends with nicknames. 2. **Make a bet** against a friend at the table (hit 🎲 Challenge next to their name). You lock `stake + 10% bond`. 3. Your friend **accepts** by locking the same amount. 4. After the game, **both players report** `a`, `b` or `draw`. - **Same report:** paid instantly, both bonds back, no fees. - **Different reports:** the bet goes to the judges. - The judges are **fixed when the bet is accepted**: every other member of the table at that moment. Both players see the panel before locking money, and nobody can add friends later to swing a vote. 5. **Judges vote.** The moment one result has a strict majority, the bet settles: - The pot goes to the winner (or back to both players on a draw), minus a **1% judge fee**. - A player whose report lost the vote **forfeits their bond**: half to the honest player, half to the judges. - Judges who voted with the majority split the fee and their half of the bond. 6. **No majority within 48 hours?** Anyone can trigger a full refund, bonds included. 7. **No-shows:** if one player reports and the other goes quiet for 24 hours, either player can escalate to the judges. ### The social bits - **Open challenges:** bet against `anyone` and the first table member to accept plays you. - **Decline:** the challenged player can turn a bet down; the challenger is refunded. - **Activity feed** per table: challenges, results, disputes and 🚩 rulings, newest first. - **Leaderboard honours:** 👑 for the table leader, 🔥 for a 3+ win streak, ⚖️ for trusted judges, 🚩 for lost disputes. - **Head-to-head records** and a **🔁 Run it back** rematch button on every settled bet. - **Your move** (web app): one list of every bet at your tables that's waiting on you: accept, report, join or judge. ### Group bets (poker night, tournaments, quizzes) 1v1 isn't enough for a poker night, so Tavern Wagers also does **group bets** for 3 to 20 players. - Everyone locks the same stake + 10% bond. The game goes live when all invited players have joined. - The pot pays out by finishing position: **winner takes all**, **60/40**, or **50/30/20** (any split that adds up to 100). - After the game, **every player reports the top places**. All agree → instant payout. Anyone disagrees → the judges decide. - **There's no dealer with all the power.** The judges are the table members who are *not* playing, and a result needs a strict majority of them. A bribe has to buy several people, not one. - **3 judges minimum, by default.** If too many people want to play, the game refuses to start unless the creator explicitly opts in, and then shows a permanent ⚠️ warning. The idea: rotate who sits out and judges each game. - Any player whose report loses the vote forfeits their bond (half to honest players, half to judges) and gets a 🚩. ### Example Alice and Bob each lock 5 GNOT + 0.5 GNOT bond. Alice won, but Bob claims he did. Two of three judges vote "Alice won". | Who | Gets | Why | |---|---|---| | Alice | 9.9 GNOT | the pot minus the 1% judge fee | | Alice | 0.5 GNOT | her bond back | | Alice | 0.25 GNOT | half of Bob's forfeited bond | | Judge 1 | 0.175 GNOT | half of (fee + other half of Bob's bond) | | Judge 2 | 0.175 GNOT | same | | Bob | 0 | lost the bet and the bond, 🚩 on the leaderboard | Total paid out: 11 GNOT = exactly what went in. ## Why Gno.land - **The rules are the code.** Anyone can read the realm's source on-chain before putting money in. - **The pot is held by the realm**, not a person or a company. - **Every table renders itself** on gnoweb (leaderboards, bets, votes and payouts) with action links for every step. No separate backend. ## Realm API | Function | Who | What | |---|---|---| | `CreateTable(name, nickname)` | anyone | opens a table, you're the owner | | `AddMember(tableID, address, nickname)` | table owner | adds a friend | | `SetNickname(tableID, nickname)` | member | changes your nickname | | `LeaveTable(tableID)` | member | leaves (not while playing or judging an unfinished bet) | | `RemoveMember(tableID, address)` | table owner | removes someone with no unfinished bets | | `CreateBet(tableID, title, opponentName, stake)` + send `stake*1.1` ugnot | member | challenges another member by nickname (or address), or `anyone` for an open challenge | | `AcceptBet(betID)` + send `stake*1.1` ugnot | player B | accepts the challenge | | `CancelBet(betID)` | player A | takes back an unaccepted bet | | `DeclineBet(betID)` | player B | turns the challenge down, A is refunded | | `Report(betID, "a"/"b"/"draw")` | players | reports the result | | `Escalate(betID)` | players | sends a no-show to the judges after 24h | | `Vote(betID, "a"/"b"/"draw")` | judges | votes on a disputed bet | | `ExpireDispute(betID)` | anyone | refunds everyone if judges miss the 48h deadline | | `CreatePool(tableID, title, players, stake, payout, acceptFewJudges)` + send `stake*1.1` | member | starts a group bet; `players` = the other players' nicknames, `payout` = `"100"`, `"60,40"`, … | | `JoinPool(poolID)` + send `stake*1.1` | invited player | locks your stake | | `CancelPool(poolID)` | creator | calls it off before everyone joined, refunds all | | `ReportPool(poolID, "Alice,Bob")` | players | reports the paid places, best first | | `EscalatePool(poolID)` | players | sends no-shows to the judges after 24h | | `VotePool(poolID, "Alice,Bob")` | judges | votes on a disputed group bet | | `ExpirePool(poolID)` | anyone | refunds everyone if judges miss the deadline | Pages: `:` (home), `:table/`, `:bet/`, `:pool/`. ## Deployment - Network: Gno.land testnet **onyx-1** - Realm: `gno.land/r/g1sgp0eyezdescdtzd32n2vdktazva4nyt9ppmcx/tavernwagers/v5` - Page: https://onyx.testnets.gno.land/r/g1sgp0eyezdescdtzd32n2vdktazva4nyt9ppmcx/tavernwagers/v5 - Submitted: (pending; v4 is in block 1391171, tx `MHTx2DCVdZQgrRHA9Oy8qL+mtDgEL7w4CqSCw1k9E48=`) Onyx parks new packages until its package approver enables them, so the page may show "Not Yet Enabled" for a while after deploying. ## Web app `web/` is a no-build web app (plain HTML/CSS/JS) on top of the realm: it reads tables and bets through the realm's JSON views (`TablesJSON`, `MyTablesJSON`, `TableJSON`, `BetJSON`, queried with `vm/qeval`) and sends every action through the [Adena](https://adena.app) wallet. Players get a bet form with an opponent picker and the exact amount to lock, one-click accept/report/vote buttons that only show when it's your move, and a head-to-head "versus" view of each bet. ```sh python3 -m http.server 8080 -d web # then open http://localhost:8080 ``` Pick **Testnet**, **Local (gnodev)** or **Demo** in the top bar. Demo mode uses sample data shaped exactly like the realm's JSON (see `web/demo.js`), so anyone can click through every screen, including a live dispute and an open group bet, without a wallet. The hosted app falls back to it automatically while the testnet package waits for approval. The gnoweb pages work on their own too: every action there is a pre-filled transaction link. ## Run it locally Requires the Gno toolchain v1.8.0 (`gno`, `gnokey`, `gnodev`). ```sh gno test -v . # unit tests bash scripts/demo-keys.sh # creates 5 demo accounts (once) bash scripts/dev.sh # starts the local chain; leave it running # in another terminal: bash scripts/demo-scenario.sh # plays a full story: honest bet, a lie caught by judges, an open challenge # open http://localhost:8888/r/g1sgp0eyezdescdtzd32n2vdktazva4nyt9ppmcx/tavernwagers/v5 ``` To play the same story on the real testnet (small stakes) once the package is enabled: ```sh bash scripts/testnet-demo.sh # funds the demo accounts from your key, then runs the scenario on onyx-1 ``` ## Tests `wagers_test.gno` covers an agreed result, a liar losing their bond, a draw where both players lied, an expired vote, a no-show escalation, cancellation and input validation, a table with no possible judges, nicknames, judges being fixed at accept time, declines, stake limits, open challenges, win streaks, the activity feed, leaving and removing members, JSON views, page rendering, and group bets (agreed winner-takes-all, a disputed 60/40 split with a liar, no-shows, escalation, expiry, validation and cancellation). Every settlement test checks that the coins paid out equal the coins paid in. ## Security notes The full threat model (attack → mitigation → what's left) and the payout math are in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). - **Coins in = coins out.** Every settlement path (agreed, disputed, draw, refund, cancel, decline) is tested to pay out exactly what was locked; rounding dust goes to a named recipient, never stays in the realm. - **Only real users can lock money.** Every function that reads the sent coins checks `IsUserCall()`, so another realm or a `maketx run` script can't fake a deposit. - **The sent amount must be exact** (stake + 10% bond), in `ugnot` only. - **Judges can't be stacked after the fact.** The panel is snapshotted when the bet is accepted (1v1) or when the last player joins (group bet). - **Players can't judge their own game**, and each judge votes once before a deadline. - **Bounded work.** Tables cap at 50 members, group bets at 20 players, stakes at 1 billion GNOT (so pots can't overflow), and pages and JSON views show the newest 30 items. - **Input hygiene.** Titles and names reject control characters, nicknames are limited to letters, numbers, spaces and `- _ .`, and everything rendered to markdown is escaped. ## Limits (honest ones) - Judges can collude. The bond makes lying expensive, but a table full of bad friends can still out-vote you. Tavern Wagers makes trust between friends fair and permanent; it doesn't replace it. - The realm can't see the real world. Results come from players and judges, never from an outside data feed.

# TavernBoard realm

TavernBoard is a community message board realm for Gno.land, built for the
Gnome Tavern Hackathon. Anyone can post a short message on chain, and anyone
can cheer (like) a message once. The board renders as Markdown through
gnoweb, newest first. There is no admin, no delete, and no edit.

- Realm path: `gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard`
- Package name: `tavernboard`
- Network target: Gno.land Onyx testnet, chain ID `onyx-1`
- RPC: `https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443` (alias `https://rpc.latest.testnets.gno.land:443`)
- Faucet: `https://faucet.gno.land` (Onyx Faucet, chain `onyx-1`)
- Gnoweb (after deploy): `https://onyx.testnets.gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard`

Status: written, unit tested (6 tests pass), and proven end to end on a
local gnodev chain (3 posts, 1 cheer, renders and queries verified). Testnet
deploy is pending faucet funding: the faucet needs a captcha solved in a
browser. See REALM-RESULT.md for the full record and the exact deploy steps
below.

## API

State-mutating (crossing) functions, called with `gnokey maketx call` or a
wallet such as Adena:

- `PostMessage(text string) int` - posts a message from the caller and
  returns its ID. IDs start at 0 and never change. Panics if the text is
  empty or longer than 280 bytes.
- `LikeMessage(id int) int` - cheers a message. Each address can cheer a
  given message at most once. Returns the new cheer count. Panics on an
  unknown ID or a repeat cheer.

Read-only functions, safe for queries (no transaction, no gas):

- `MessageCount() int` - how many messages have been posted.
- `GetMessage(id int) (author string, text string, height int64, likes int)`
  - one message in full. Panics on an unknown ID.
- `HasLiked(id int, who address) bool` - whether an address cheered a
  message. Panics on an unknown ID.
- `Render(path string) string` - Markdown for gnoweb. Root (`""` or `"/"`)
  lists the newest 50 messages; `"/<id>"` shows one message.

Each message stores: author address, text, block height at posting time,
cheer count, and the set of addresses that cheered it.

Gas note: posting costs more gas as the board grows (about 2.3M gas for the
first post, about 2.9M by the third in local testing). Use
`-gas-wanted 5000000 -gas-fee 5000ugnot` for calls to stay safe.

## Run locally (no testnet needed)

Toolchain used here: `gno`, `gnokey`, `gnodev` v1.8.0 in
`~/workspace/gno-tools/bin`, with `GNOROOT=~/workspace/gno-tools/gno`
(a v1.8.0 checkout of github.com/gnolang/gno; the `gno` CLI needs the
stdlib sources from the repo).

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/workspace/gno-tools/bin:$PATH"
export GNOROOT="$HOME/workspace/gno-tools/gno"
cd ~/workspace/hackathons/gnome-tavern-2026-11-26/realm

gno fmt -w ./...
gno lint ./...

  -add-account g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl=100000000000ugnot .

# In another terminal:
gnokey query vm/qrender -data "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard:" -remote http://127.0.0.1:26657
```

1. Fund the key (browser step, captcha required). Go to
   https://faucet.gno.land, choose the Onyx Faucet (chain `onyx-1`), paste
   `g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl`, solve the captcha, submit.
   100 GNOT is more than enough. Tokens arrive in seconds.

2. Confirm the funds landed:

```bash

  -remote https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443
```

3. Deploy the realm (run from this directory; gnokey asks for the key
   password from `keyfile-info.txt`):

```bash

  -pkgpath "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard" \
  -pkgdir . \

  -chainid onyx-1 -remote https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443 \
  -home ./.gnokey-home tavernboard-dev
```

4. Wait a few seconds: the testnet enables a new package shortly after
   `addpkg`. If calls fail with "package not known", wait and retry. If it
   still fails after a minute, look up the exact package path at
   https://gpas.latest.testnets.gno.land for the refusal reason.

5. Post and cheer:

```bash
gnokey maketx call -pkgpath "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard" \
  -func PostMessage -args "Welcome to TavernBoard" \
  -gas-fee 5000ugnot -gas-wanted 5000000 -chainid onyx-1 \
  -remote https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443 -home ./.gnokey-home tavernboard-dev

gnokey maketx call -pkgpath "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard" \
  -func LikeMessage -args "0" \
  -gas-fee 5000ugnot -gas-wanted 5000000 -chainid onyx-1 \
  -remote https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443 -home ./.gnokey-home tavernboard-dev
```

6. View it: https://onyx.testnets.gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard
   (single message: append `:/0`, `:/1`, and so on).

Note for this VM: `gnokey` cannot reach the testnet RPC from here (the
egress proxy breaks Go TLS; `curl` queries work, `gnokey` broadcasts do
not). Run the deploy commands from a normal machine, or see
REALM-RESULT.md for details.

## Reading state from a front end

- Render (Markdown, best for display): ABCI query path `vm/qrender`, data
  `gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard:` for the
  board, or `.../tavernboard:/<id>` for one message. With gnokey:
  `gnokey query vm/qrender -data "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard:" -remote https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443`
- Eval (typed values, best for app logic): ABCI query path `vm/qeval`, data
  `gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard.MessageCount()`,
  `.../tavernboard.GetMessage(0)`, `.../tavernboard.HasLiked(0, "g1...")`.
  Loop `GetMessage(i)` for `i` in `0..MessageCount()-1` to rebuild the
  board in the UI.
- Writes: MsgCall to `PostMessage` / `LikeMessage` via Adena wallet or
  gnokey. The gnoweb Actions tab for the realm shows a form per function
  plus the equivalent gnokey command.

## Files

- `tavernboard.gno` - the realm.
- `tavernboard_test.gno` - unit tests (`gno test`).
- `gnomod.toml` - module path and Gno version (0.9).
- `local-proof.log` - full local chain proof (deploy, posts, cheer, renders).
- `REALM-RESULT.md` - research notes, test results, deployment status.
- `keyfile-info.txt` - testnet key record (chmod 600, keep private).
- `.gnokey-home/` - encrypted gnokey keybase for `tavernboard-dev`
  (chmod 700). Recoverable from `keyfile-info.txt` with
  `gnokey add tavernboard-dev --recover -home <dir>` (verified).
- `.gnokey-home-superseded/` - keybase of a superseded first key that was
  never funded or deployed. Safe to delete.

files.body:
# TavernBoard realm: result record

Date: 2026-11-26. Project: TavernBoard, a community message board realm on
Gno.land for the Gnome Tavern Hackathon. Work directory:
`~/workspace/hackathons/gnome-tavern-2026-11-26/realm/`.

## Bottom line

- Realm written, formatted, linted, and unit tested: 6 of 6 tests pass.
- Proven end to end on a local gnodev chain: deployed at its real path,
  3 messages posted, 1 cheer recorded, renders and typed queries verified
  (tx hashes below).
- NOT deployed to testnet yet. Two blockers, both outside the code:
  1. Funding: the Onyx faucet requires solving an hCaptcha in a browser.
     A direct API POST without a captcha token produced no funds (request
     timed out, balance still empty). This subagent has no live browser.
  2. Networking: `gnokey` cannot reach the testnet RPC from this VM. Its
     Go TLS handshake fails through the VM egress proxy
     ("tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake"), while
     `curl` queries through the same proxy work. So even a funded key
     could not broadcast with gnokey from here without extra plumbing.
- One browser faucet visit by Ibrahim plus the deploy commands in
  README.md (run from any normal machine) finishes the testnet launch.
  Nothing else is missing: key, code, tests, and commands are ready.

## Research summary

Sources: docs.gno.land Getting started, Quick Start, Gno networks, and
Interact with gnokey pages (fetched 2026-11-26), plus live RPC checks.

Networks:

| Network | Chain ID | RPC | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local (gnodev) | `dev` | `http://localhost:26657` | gnoweb at `http://localhost:8888`, keys auto-funded |
| Onyx testnet (current) | `onyx-1` | `https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443` | alias `https://rpc.latest.testnets.gno.land:443` always points at the current testnet |
| Mainnet | `gnoland-1` | `https://rpc.gno.land:443` | no faucet, real GNOT. Not used here. |

Live check on 2026-11-26 about 12:49 UTC: Onyx RPC `/status` reported
network `onyx-1`, height 1426694, not catching up. Onyx launched
2026-09-28, runs mainnet code as release candidates, state persists across
upgrades. Staging is down since 2026-07-10; Pearl and older testnets are
retired.

Faucet: https://faucet.gno.land (Onyx Faucet, chain `onyx-1`, amounts
100/200/300 GNOT, hCaptcha protected). API base
`https://faucet.onyx.testnets.gno.land` accepts POSTs from the web UI with
a captcha token. `https://onyx.testnets.gno.land/faucet` redirects to the
same hub.

Gnoweb URL format: `https://<host>/r/<namespace>/<name>` for the realm
page, with `:/<path>` appended for Render subpaths (for example
`.../tavernboard:/0`). Testnet hosts: `onyx.testnets.gno.land` and
`latest.testnets.gno.land`. Every realm page has Content (Render output),
Source, and Actions tabs. Actions shows a wallet form and the equivalent
gnokey command per exported crossing function.

Realm path format: `gno.land/r/<namespace>/<name>` for realms (stateful),
`gno.land/p/...` for pure packages. The simplest namespace is the
deployer's own address, `gno.land/r/<g1-address>/...`, which needs no
registration. Named namespaces need on-chain registration first. The
`gnomod.toml` module field must match the `-pkgpath` used at deploy.

gnokey essentials:

- `gnokey add <name>` creates a key (prompts for password, prints a
  24-word mnemonic). `-home` selects the keybase directory,
  `-insecure-password-stdin` reads the password from stdin (used here for
  scripted setup; the password itself is only in `keyfile-info.txt`).
- Deploy: `gnokey maketx addpkg -pkgpath <path> -pkgdir . -gas-fee
  5000ugnot -gas-wanted 5000000 -chainid <id> -remote <rpc> <key>`.
  Deploys also lock a storage deposit of 100ugnot per byte of code and
  state, charged on top of the gas fee.
- Call: `gnokey maketx call -pkgpath <path> -func <Fn> -args <arg> ...
  -gas-fee <fee> -gas-wanted <gas> -chainid <id> -remote <rpc> <key>`.
  Gas price floor is 1ugnot per 1000 gas, so fee must be at least
  gas-wanted/1000 ugnot.
- Queries need no key: `gnokey query bank/balances/<addr> -remote <rpc>`,
  `gnokey query vm/qrender -data "<pkgpath>:" -remote <rpc>`,
  `gnokey query vm/qeval -data "<pkgpath>.<Expr>" -remote <rpc>`.
- After `addpkg`, the testnet enables the package a few seconds later.
  Refusal reasons are listed by exact package path at
  https://gpas.latest.testnets.gno.land.

Gno language notes (0.9, toolchain v1.8.0):

- State-mutating exported functions are "crossing functions": first
  parameter `cur realm`, called as `Fn(cross(cur), ...)` from Gno code or
  automatically by gnokey MsgCall. Author identity:
  `cur.Previous().Address()` after checking `cur.IsCurrent()`.
- Block height: `chain/runtime.ChainHeight()` (int64). There is no block
  time helper in `chain/runtime`; height is the deterministic stamp.
- Top-level vars persist to chain state after each transaction.
- `Render(path string) string` returns Markdown for gnoweb.
- Tests: `func TestX(cur realm, t *testing.T)`. Panics raised inside a
  crossing call abort the test run and cannot be recovered; panics in
  plain (non-crossing) functions can. The realm therefore keeps its
  validation in small non-crossing helpers (`cleanText`, `checkID`,
  `checkCanLike`) that the crossing functions call, so the rules are
  unit testable. This matches the pattern in the upstream coins realm
  tests, which only recover panics from `Render`.

Toolchain on this VM:

- `go version`: Go is NOT installed on this VM.
- Installed the official prebuilt toolchain v1.8.0 with
  `misc/install.sh --dir ~/workspace/gno-tools/bin` (sha256 verified by
  the installer): `gno`, `gnokey`, `gnodev`, `gnoweb`. Building from
  source was not attempted: no Go toolchain, and the prebuilt installer
  is the documented path. No execution-risk block was hit.
- Gotcha: the prebuilt `gno` binary looks for stdlib sources at its CI
  build path. Fixed by cloning the repo (tag v1.8.0, shallow, 196 MB) to
  `~/workspace/gno-tools/gno` and setting `GNOROOT` to it. With that,
  `gno fmt/lint/test` and `gnodev` all work.
- Everything lives under `~/workspace/gno-tools/`; no system paths were
  modified.

## Realm design

File `tavernboard.gno`, package `tavernboard`, module
`gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard`.

- `type Message struct { Author address; Text string; Height int64;
  Likes int; LikedBy map[address]bool }`, stored in `var messages
  []Message`. Message ID = slice index (0-based, stable forever).
- `PostMessage(cur realm, text string) int`: crossing. Trims text,
  panics on empty or over 280 bytes (`MaxMessageLen`), stamps author
  from `cur.Previous().Address()` and height from
  `runtime.ChainHeight()`, appends, returns the new ID.
- `LikeMessage(cur realm, id int) int`: crossing. Panics on unknown ID
  or if the caller already cheered; otherwise records the cheer and
  returns the new count. One cheer per address per message.
- `MessageCount() int`, `GetMessage(id) (string, string, int64, int)`,
  `HasLiked(id, who) bool`: read-only helpers for queries and front ends.
- `Render(path)`: root lists the newest 50 messages (`MaxMessagesShown`)
  with author (shortened), block height, cheer count, and text with
  newlines folded so posts cannot break the layout. `"/<id>"` shows one
  message; unknown paths render a friendly not-found page instead of
  panicking.
- No admin, no delete, no edit, no fees, no external calls. Imports only
  `chain/runtime`, `strconv`, `strings`.

## Test results

`gno fmt -w ./...` applied, `gno lint ./...` clean, `gno test -v ./...`:

- TestPostMessage: PASS (IDs, trimming, author, height, counts)
- TestPostMessageRejectsBadText: PASS (empty, blank, 281 bytes rejected;
  exactly 280 bytes accepted)
- TestLikeMessage: PASS (cheer once, HasLiked, repeat rejected)
- TestLikeMessageOtherAuthor: PASS (cheering another author's post)
- TestBadIDs: PASS (unknown and negative IDs rejected everywhere)
- TestRender: PASS (empty board, newest-first order, cheer counts,
  single-message view, not-found pages)

6 passed, 0 failed.

## Local deployment proof (gnodev dev chain)

Started `gnodev local -no-watch` with the realm directory as workspace,
deploy key and premine set to the tavernboard-dev address (100 GNOT
premine = 100000000000ugnot). Chain ID `dev`, RPC `http://127.0.0.1:26657`,
gnoweb `http://127.0.0.1:8888`. Full output in `local-proof.log`.

| Action | Result | Height | Gas used | Total cost | Tx hash |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PostMessage "Welcome to TavernBoard, our community board for the Gnome Tavern Hackathon" | id 0 | 3 | 2245970 | 144700ugnot | `T3B1UgP0Qv23QqvH8qjHP0L4F6/YB7ZRW3QxBt/UhMo=` |
| PostMessage "Built with Gno realms: post a message, cheer the ones you like" | id 1 | 5 | 2566813 | 112000ugnot | `gavk9w2xiOLKZqcAOuruWFzlvXmuxwnYs/hYM/S/ddM=` |
| PostMessage "Third round is on the board. Pull up a stool and say hello" | id 2 | 7 | 2856077 | 111600ugnot | `pBQJP+ALqh16uzThN33Hf+iExHRtvf70MEZK7mY4/O8=` |
| LikeMessage(0) | 1 cheer | 9 | 2406415 | 20300ugnot | `rGG+LPp09PESFvtycarT2XN50Bkh3N4owK9mY0Qlo/s=` |

Queries verified on the same chain: `MessageCount()` = 3;
`GetMessage(0)` = (g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl, welcome text,
height 3, likes 1); `HasLiked(0, author)` = true. `Render` lists message
2, 1, 0 in that order with cheer counts 0, 0, 1; `Render("/0")` shows
only message 0. Gnoweb served the same content at
`http://127.0.0.1:8888/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard`
(HTTP 200, "Total messages: 3"). Balance went from 99997713700ugnot to
99997325100ugnot, a spend of exactly 388600ugnot, matching the four tx
costs above.

Two local lessons, now handled: (1) PostMessage needs more than 2M gas;
2M gas-wanted failed in simulation, 4M succeeded. Use 5M on testnet.
(2) gnodev watches the package directory and reloads on any file change,
including log files written there; during reloads RPC returns 502. Run
gnodev with `-no-watch` and keep scratch files out of the realm dir.

## Testnet deployment status: not deployed (honest fallback)

Key created (testnet only): name `tavernboard-dev`, address
`g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl`. Mnemonic and password are
recorded only in `keyfile-info.txt` (chmod 600) in the realm directory;
they are not in this report. The encrypted keybase is at
`realm/.gnokey-home` (chmod 700) and can be recreated from
`keyfile-info.txt` with `gnokey add tavernboard-dev --recover`.
Recovery was verified at creation: recovering from the recorded mnemonic
reproduces the same address.

Superseded first key: an earlier key (`g1v397843gg6lszdvtfz6ts6ef6tmvq8g6q7slym`)
was created first, but its mnemonic was captured incorrectly (the warning
sentence was recorded instead of the 24-word phrase). A recovery test
caught this before anything depended on it. That key was never funded and
never deployed; the realm path, local proof, and all commands were redone
with the current key above. The old encrypted keybase is preserved at
`realm/.gnokey-home-superseded` (chmod 700) and can be deleted.

Funding attempts and evidence:

- Balance checks via curl ABCI query on
  `https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land`: the superseded address showed
  balance data `""` (zero) and account `null` (does not exist yet); the
  current address `g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl` likewise
  shows balance data `""`. Expected for fresh, unfunded keys.
- Faucet API attempt (for the superseded address, before recreation):
  POST `https://faucet.onyx.testnets.gno.land` with
  `{"address":"g1v397843gg6lszdvtfz6ts6ef6tmvq8g6q7slym","amount":100}`
  and no captcha token: request timed out (HTTP 000 after 30s), balance
  unchanged. The web UI requires an hCaptcha token, which needs a human
  in a browser. No funds were obtained and none were faked.
- gnokey to testnet RPC from this VM:
  `gnokey query bank/balances/... -remote https://rpc.latest.testnets.gno.land`
  fails with "tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake"
  (VM egress proxy intercepts direct TLS; curl works because it uses the
  proxy properly). So `addpkg` broadcasts cannot run from this VM with
  gnokey as-is.

What Ibrahim needs to do (about 2 minutes):

1. Open https://faucet.gno.land, pick Onyx Faucet (onyx-1), paste
   `g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl`, solve captcha, submit

   100ugnot/byte for about 7 KB of code and state, plus small gas fees).

3. Confirm at https://onyx.testnets.gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard

Testnet only throughout. No mainnet interaction, no real funds, no keys
requested from anyone.

## Endpoints for the front end

- RPC: `https://rpc.onyx.testnets.gno.land:443` (alias

## Exact commands used (key steps)

```bash
gnokey maketx call -pkgpath "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard" -func PostMessage -args "..." -gas-fee 4000ugnot -gas-wanted 4000000 -chainid dev -remote http://127.0.0.1:26657 -home ./.gnokey-home -insecure-password-stdin tavernboard-dev
gnokey maketx call -pkgpath "gno.land/r/g1q5ra3080jnhk8skw664lyz9p97t7reddup89rl/tavernboard" -func LikeMessage -args "0" -gas-fee 4000ugnot -gas-wanted 4000000 -chainid dev -remote http://127.0.0.1:26657 -home ./.gnokey-home -insecure-password-stdin tavernboard-dev
```

- `realm/tavernboard_test.gno` - unit tests.
